newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal closes higher on China rumors.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal closes higher on China rumors.

text.p: Early commercial demand and late fund buying boosted CBOT soymeal futures to a higher close with rumors China again was seeking soymeal, the catalyst for the gains, traders said.
"There was commercial buying so some thought maybe there was something to it (the China rumor)," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Cargill Inc bought 400 lots of March and Continental Grain bought 150 lots of December, traders said.
Support also came from a weekly export report, a listing with more reliable bullish input, the traders said.

USDA early Monday released weekly export inspections data which showed the soybean tally for the week ended December 12 at 36.236 million bushels, above trade expectations of 20 million to 25 million bushels.
Cold weather in the U.S. which led to ideas for a hike in feed usage by the nation's livestock also lifted futures.
Soyoil closed mixed and was pressured by meal/oil spreading, the traders said.
Soymeal closed $1.10 to $4.80 per ton higher, with December up $4.80 at $242.20. Soyoil was 0.03 cent per lb lower to 0.04 higher, with December down 0.02 at 23.13.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, above the 15,005 traded Friday, according to the CBOT.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 16,000 contracts, above 15,163 traded Friday.
